'''Hans Jakob Reiter''' (26 November 1921 – 13 August 1992) was an Austrian mathematician working in analysis.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Hlawka | first1=E. | title=Hans J. Reiter | year=1992 | journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik | issn=0026-9255 | volume=114 | issue=3–4 | pages=171–173 | doi=10.1007/BF01299378| s2cid=121321993 }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Derighetti | first1=Antoine | title=On the mathematical work of Hans Reiter | doi=10.1007/BF01299379 |mr=1203970 | year=1992 | journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik | issn=0026-9255 | volume=114 | issue=3 | pages=175–182| s2cid=121582851 }}</ref>

Because of the [[Anschluss]], Hans Reiter had to leave his hometown before his [[Matura]]. Via Italy he was able to emigrate to Brazil, where he studied under [[André Weil]]. In 1953 he received his PhD from [[Rice University]] under [[Szolem Mandelbrojt]] with thesis ''Investigations in harmonic analysis''.<ref>[http://scholarship.rice.edu/handle/1911/18417 Hans J. Reiter's thesis from Rice University's Electronic Theses and Dissertations]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Reiter, H. J.|title=Investigations in harmonic analysis|journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1952|volume=73|issue=3|pages=401–427|mr=0051341|doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-1952-0051341-6|doi-access=free|hdl=1911/18417|hdl-access=free}}</ref> In 1952 he became an assistant at the [[University of Vienna]] and in 1971 obtained a professorial chair there, after years in various foreign academic positions, including an interval from 1964 to 1971 as a professor at the [[University of Utrecht]]. Reiter's doctoral students include [[Hans Georg Feichtinger]].

Reiter wrote the widely used textbook ''Classical Harmonic Analysis and Locally Compact Groups''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oemg.ac.at/Tagungen/2001/KuehlerAbschied.pdf|title="Kühler Abschied von Europa" – Wien 1938 und der Exodus der Mathematik|year=2001|publisher=Austrian Mathematical Society|page=124}}</ref>
